question: I'm building a little space shooter in the browser. Where should I even start?
lines: {"say": "Start with a game loop, then draw and move your ship."}
{"say": "Use the browser's built-in canvas for drawing, and make a game loop update movement before redrawing each frame."}
{"say": "Once movement feels good, add shots fired with the space bar and one enemy drifting toward you."}
{"say": "Next, check whether shots overlap enemies, remove anything hit, and increase the score."}
{"say": "Aim for one playable minute before adding fancy graphics, sound, or more enemy types."}

question: Nice. I want player accounts and a global high score board. What stack would you use?
lines: {"say": "Use TypeScript and Canvas, with Supabase for accounts, PostgreSQL leaderboards, and server-side score validation."}
{"say": "Keep your canvas game, add TypeScript with Vite, and deploy the browser app on Cloudflare Pages."}
{"say": "Use Supabase Auth for signups and login, so you don't have to manage passwords yourself."}
{"say": "Store player profiles and scores in Supabase Postgres, with an index for fetching the highest scores quickly."}
{"say": "Submit scores through a Supabase Edge Function that verifies login and rejects obviously impossible results."}
{"say": "Use database access policies to allow public leaderboard reads but block direct score writes from players."}
{"say": "Browser scores are still forgeable; if competition gets serious, validate gameplay replays rather than trusting submitted totals."}

question: Where would I actually host all of this?
lines: {"say": "Host the game on Cloudflare Pages and the backend on Supabase."}
{"say": "First, connect your Git repository to Cloudflare Pages so each push can automatically deploy your game."}
{"say": "Create one Supabase project to host authentication, your database, and the score validation function."}
{"say": "Your browser calls that function to submit scores, and the function writes accepted results into the database."}
{"say": "Put only Supabase's public project settings in your frontend; keep privileged keys inside the hosted function."}
{"say": "Start with their free tiers, check current limits, and add a custom domain when you're ready."}
{"say": "You won't need to rent a server or manage operating system updates for this setup."}

question: Okay, big change. I want it multiplayer, so friends can fly together in real time. What changes?
lines: {"say": "Real-time multiplayer means moving game state off the browser and onto a server that players share."}
{"say": "The server runs the authoritative game loop, so every player's client just sends inputs and renders what it receives."}
{"say": "Clients predict their own movement locally so controls still feel instant despite network delay."}
{"say": "Interpolate other players' positions between snapshots so remote ships glide instead of teleporting."}
{"say": "Run the WebSocket server on Cloudflare Durable Objects, one per game room, keeping state in memory."}
{"say": "Friends join through a room code; the first player creates it and shares the link with the group."}
{"say": "Add a dedicated Colyseus game server on Fly.io to own movement, enemies, and collisions for each match."}
{"say": "Each player's browser sends controls over WebSockets; the server broadcasts the shared game state."}
{"say": "Keep Cloudflare Pages for hosting the game files, and Supabase for accounts and persistent scores, not live movement."}
{"say": "Start with one invite-only room for two friends, adding client prediction and interpolation to hide network delays."}
{"say": "Have the game server verify login tokens and save final scores, replacing score submissions from the browser."}
{"say": "Run a single server near your players initially; add regional hosting and room allocation when demand grows."}
